title: Learn a route in a building
description: Learn the way from an entrance to a room, and back, without the signs if they fail.
oneStarDescription: Walk from the entrance to the room and name two landmarks.
twoStarDescription: Walk back and say the landmarks in reverse.
threeStarDescription: Say how you would leave if your usual corridor were closed.

title: Mend a bicycle puncture
description: Find a hole in a bicycle inner tube, patch it, and show that it holds air.
oneStarDescription: Remove the wheel if you need to, take out the tube, and find the hole with water or by feeling the escaping air.
twoStarDescription: Apply a patch kit as its own instructions say, and wait as those instructions say.
threeStarDescription: Refit the tube without pinching it, inflate within the tire's range, and show that it still holds after a few minutes.

title: Mend a small seam
description: Close a short split seam by hand so the repair lies flat.
oneStarDescription: Sew a short split so the original edges meet and the thread is fastened at both ends.
twoStarDescription: Turn the cloth right side out and show that the mend does not leave a twist or an open gap.
threeStarDescription: Point to a hole or a worn-out area you would not mend this way, and say why.

title: Mix a color you can match
description: Mix a paint or a digital color until it is closer to a sample than your first try.
oneStarDescription: Mix a color aimed at a sample you can see.
twoStarDescription: Say whether the mix is too light, too dark, or too far toward one hue, and change only that.
threeStarDescription: Put the mix next to the sample and say what difference remains.

title: Move through a short sequence
description: Learn a short sequence of movements and repeat it without the demonstration in front of you.
oneStarDescription: Follow a short sequence from a teacher or a video you are allowed to use.
twoStarDescription: Do the sequence without watching, and name the move you forgot.
threeStarDescription: Repeat it and keep one point of form, such as a steady breath or a soft knee, and say when you lost it.

title: Name plants you can find nearby
description: Identify a plant near you with a guide, and say what you are still unsure of.
oneStarDescription: Match one plant to a guide using a leaf or a flower you can see.
twoStarDescription: Confirm or doubt the match with a second feature, such as the leaf edge or the growth habit.
threeStarDescription: Point to a plant you will not name, and say which feature is missing.

title: Negotiate a deadline
description: Ask for a deadline you can meet, and leave with a date both sides share.
oneStarDescription: Before you accept a date, say what the work includes.
twoStarDescription: Propose a date and the reason it is realistic.
threeStarDescription: Restate the agreed date and what will be ready, in a message both sides have.

title: Notice effort and ease off
description: During ordinary exercise you already do, notice when effort rises and take an easier step.
oneStarDescription: During a walk, a ride, or another familiar effort, say whether it is easy, steady, or hard.
twoStarDescription: When it becomes hard, slow down or stop, and say what you changed.
threeStarDescription: Either continue at the easier pace or end the session, and say which you chose and why.

title: Offer help that can be refused
description: Offer help in a way the other person can decline without awkwardness.
oneStarDescription: Offer a specific action, not a general 'let me know'.
twoStarDescription: Ask in a way that allows no, and stop if they decline.
threeStarDescription: If they accept, do the action you offered and check it matched what they wanted.

title: Officiate a casual game
description: Apply agreed rules in a casual game and explain one call.
oneStarDescription: Before play, state the rule you will watch and how a point starts.
twoStarDescription: Make one call during play and say the fact you saw.
threeStarDescription: Hear one objection, keep or change the call, and say why.

title: Organize files so you can find them
description: Put files where a later search by name or folder finds the one you need.
oneStarDescription: Rename one file so the name says what it is and when it is from.
twoStarDescription: Put it in a folder whose name matches the name, and find it again without browsing at random.
threeStarDescription: The next day, find the file from the name or the folder, and fix the name if you could not.

title: Pack for a specific trip
description: Pack a bag for a stated trip and show that each item has a reason.
oneStarDescription: Write the weather, the length, and one activity, then list what those require.
twoStarDescription: Pack the list and take out one item you cannot tie to the trip.
threeStarDescription: Name one thing still missing that would matter on the first day, and add it or say why you cannot.

title: Paraphrase a paragraph
description: Rewrite a paragraph in your own words without losing the claim.
oneStarDescription: Underline the sentence that carries the claim.
twoStarDescription: Rewrite the paragraph without copying a sentence, and keep the claim.
threeStarDescription: Compare the two and restore one fact you dropped.

title: Pitch a tent so it stays up
description: Pitch a tent from its own picture or instructions so the poles are seated and the door closes.
oneStarDescription: Lay the tent out and identify the door and the pole sleeves from the instructions or the color codes.
twoStarDescription: Seat the poles and close the door, and show that the inner is not twisted.
threeStarDescription: Peg or weight the side that lifts, and say what you would do if the wind increased beyond this site.

title: Place an event on a timeline
description: Put an event on a timeline with what came before and after.
oneStarDescription: Write the event and a date or period you can point to in a source.
twoStarDescription: Add one event before and one after, with their dates.
threeStarDescription: Say one way the earlier event makes the later one easier to understand, or say you see no link.

title: Pack a meal to eat later
description: Pack a meal that is still edible when you eat it, and say what you kept cold.
oneStarDescription: Choose foods that can sit until you will eat them, and leave out one that cannot.
twoStarDescription: Pack it so it does not leak, and keep the cold item cold if it needs cold.
threeStarDescription: Eat it at the planned time and write one change for next time.

title: Plan a walk you can return from
description: Plan a short walk with a turn-around time and a way back you can describe.
oneStarDescription: On a map, mark a short route and the point where you turn around.
twoStarDescription: Write the time you will turn around even if you have not finished.
threeStarDescription: Say the way back in a sentence someone else could follow, including one landmark.

title: Plan a week of meals
description: Plan several meals from food you can get, including one meal that uses leftovers.
oneStarDescription: Write three meals and the main ingredient each one needs.
twoStarDescription: Mark which meal will use food left from another, and which ingredient you still need to buy.
threeStarDescription: Replace one meal after you learn an ingredient is missing, without abandoning the other meals.

title: Plan a week with buffers
description: Put real commitments on a week and leave open time where a slip would otherwise break the next thing.
oneStarDescription: Write the commitments you cannot move, with their times.
twoStarDescription: Place one task away from a fixed commitment so a delay in the task does not collide with it.
threeStarDescription: When one block slips, move one later task and say what you dropped.

title: Play a trick-taking card game
description: Play a trick-taking game by following suit, and say who won a trick.
oneStarDescription: Play a hand in which you follow suit when you can, using the rules of one named game.
twoStarDescription: Point to a trick and say which card won it under those rules.
threeStarDescription: Before you play one card, say what you hope it will do, then say whether it did.

title: Play a game of chess
description: Play chess to checkmate or another agreed end, using a reference for any move you are unsure of.
oneStarDescription: Set up the pieces from a diagram and say which side moves first.
twoStarDescription: Play until checkmate, stalemate, resignation, or an agreed draw, and name which ending it was.
threeStarDescription: Point to one of your moves that left a piece open, and say what you could have done instead.

title: Play a game of dominoes
description: Play a matching domino game to an empty hand or a blocked board.
oneStarDescription: Play tiles that match the open ends, using one named ruleset.
twoStarDescription: Show either a score you recorded or a board where nobody can play.
threeStarDescription: Point to a tile you played and one you wish you had saved.

title: Play draughts
description: Play draughts or checkers to a finish, including one promotion if the game reaches it.
oneStarDescription: Play several moves that obey the direction and the capture rule you are using.
twoStarDescription: When a capture is available, take it if your rules require it, and show the position after.
threeStarDescription: Play to a win, a loss, or a position you both agree is drawn, and name one move you would change.

title: Play a game of Go
description: Play Go on a small board, capture or surround, and count the result with a reference.
oneStarDescription: Play on a small board with the liberty rule in front of you, and show one capture or say why there was none.
twoStarDescription: Play until both players pass, and point to one group that lived or died.
threeStarDescription: Count the result with a reference or a stronger player, and say one point you would have played differently.

title: Play mancala
description: Play a mancala game by sowing seeds and say how a turn ends.
oneStarDescription: Sow the seeds from one pit in the direction your rules use.
twoStarDescription: Play a turn that ends in a capture or an extra turn if the rules give one, and say which happened.
threeStarDescription: Play until the rules say the game is over, and count the stores with the other player.

title: Polish a pair of shoes
description: Clean and polish leather shoes so the dull area you started with looks even.
oneStarDescription: Remove dried dirt and let the shoe dry if it was wet.
twoStarDescription: Apply a thin coat of polish suited to the shoe and buff one shoe to an even look.
threeStarDescription: Do the second shoe and say which scuff you did not try to hide because it is damage, not dirt.

title: Practice an explanation out loud
description: Practice a short explanation aloud and fix the sentence where you stumble.
oneStarDescription: Explain a topic aloud for a minute without reading.
twoStarDescription: Note the sentence where you stopped or circled, in a few words.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite that sentence and say the explanation again, including the new line.

title: Prepare papers for a trip
description: Gather the documents a specific trip requires and note one you still need to check.
oneStarDescription: From the carrier or the border page you are using, list the documents they name.
twoStarDescription: Set out the documents you have and mark each item on the list as present or missing.
threeStarDescription: Check one expiry or validity date and say whether it covers the travel dates.

title: Protect time for one priority
description: Put one important task on the calendar and do it in that block.
oneStarDescription: Name one task that matters this week and a block long enough to start it.
twoStarDescription: Work on that task in the block and write the sentence you finished.
threeStarDescription: When something else asks for the block, either keep it or move it to a new time you write down.

title: Read a city transit map
description: Use a transit map to name a route between two stops.
oneStarDescription: Find your stop and the stop you want on a map or a posted diagram.
twoStarDescription: Name the line and the direction, and one place you would change if needed.
threeStarDescription: If a notice says the line is broken, name another way or say you would ask.

title: Read a food label for a choice
description: Use a food label to choose between two products for a reason you can point to.
oneStarDescription: On one package, point to the ingredient list and the serving the numbers refer to.
twoStarDescription: Compare two products on one fact you care about, using the same kind of serving.
threeStarDescription: Choose one product and name one fact the label does not tell you.

title: Read a household bill
description: Read a bill so you can point to the amount due, the period, and one charge you understand.
oneStarDescription: On a bill, point to the amount due and the date it refers to.
twoStarDescription: Explain one line in ordinary words and point to the meter reading or quantity if it is printed.
threeStarDescription: Circle or note one figure you cannot explain, and say who you would ask.

title: Read the scale of a map
description: Use a map scale to say whether a distance is a short walk or a long one.
oneStarDescription: Point to the scale bar or the ratio on a map.
twoStarDescription: Measure one route on the map and convert it with the scale.
threeStarDescription: Say whether that distance is a casual walk for you, and what would make the judgement wrong, such as hills the scale does not show.

title: Read a museum label
description: Read a museum label and separate what the object is from what the label claims about it.
oneStarDescription: From the label, say what the object is and where it is from.
twoStarDescription: Point to one sentence that interprets the object, not only names it.
threeStarDescription: Write a question the label does not answer.

title: Read a payslip or an invoice
description: Read a payslip or an invoice so you can point to the gross amount, a deduction or tax line, and the amount paid.
oneStarDescription: Point to the gross amount and the amount that was paid or is due.
twoStarDescription: Explain one deduction, tax, or fee in ordinary words.
threeStarDescription: Mark one figure you do not understand and write the question you would ask the payer.

title: Read a percentage in a claim
description: Turn a percentage in a real claim into a count you can picture.
oneStarDescription: Point to the percentage and say what group it is a part of.
twoStarDescription: Turn the percentage into a count out of 10 or 100, and show the arithmetic.
threeStarDescription: Name one fact the claim still needs, such as how many people were counted.

title: Read a published chart
description: Read a chart well enough to say what it compares and what it does not show.
oneStarDescription: Say what the chart measures and what each axis or category is.
twoStarDescription: Make one comparison the chart supports, and point to the marks you used.
threeStarDescription: Say one conclusion a reader might draw that the chart does not actually show.

title: Read a recipe before you start
description: Read a recipe through, set out the ingredients, and notice a missing item before you cook.
oneStarDescription: Read the recipe once before you turn on the heat.
twoStarDescription: Set out every ingredient the recipe names, or mark the one you do not have.
threeStarDescription: Either substitute an ingredient you can justify or choose not to start, and say which.

title: Read a timetable
description: Read a public timetable and pick a departure that gets you there before a deadline.
oneStarDescription: Point to the destination and the list of times on a timetable.
twoStarDescription: Choose a departure that arrives before a time you wrote down, and show the arrival.
threeStarDescription: Say what you will do if that service is late or cancelled.

title: Read a trail marker
description: Follow a trail marker you can see, and stop when the next marker is missing.
oneStarDescription: Point to a blaze, a cairn, or a sign and say what direction it gives.
twoStarDescription: Walk only as far as the next marker you can see, and show it.
threeStarDescription: If you cannot see the next marker, stop and say how you will go back to the last one.
